land.text: the English colony of Francis Willoughby ('Willoughbyland', founded 1650), around 30,000 acres (120 km2) on the Suriname River

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's English Colonial Empire row has Suriname cells in the 1650s-1660s (am-07 to check); the Dutch took it on 26 February 1667.

successors.note: Cliopatria's Republic of Suriname row starts in 1976 (146,979 km2); independence was on 25 November 1975.

capitals.name: Paramaribo (Fort Zeelandia)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Paramaribo; Fort Willoughby was renamed Fort Zeelandia in 1667. Also the seat of the merged West Indies colony of 1828-1845.

correction.text: the plantation coast of Suriname between the Corantijn and the Marowijne, the 81 Suriname cells that Cliopatria files from 1670 under its New Netherland row; the English colony it took over covered 'around 30,000 acres (120 km2)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: no Cliopatria row is called Suriname before 1976, and its 1670-1799 Suriname cells sit inside the New Netherland row (reviewed in the new-netherland dossier). Dutch from 26 February 1667. The pages give no extent for the Dutch colony, 'plantations producing sugar, coffee, cocoa, and cotton' on the coast and Indigenous peoples and Maroons inland, so the coastal belt is the researcher's reading of the Cliopatria shape (unverified: page budget). Cliopatria's two-cell dip in 1781-1787 and 1797-1799 is not on any page.

correction.text: the coastal belt under British occupation 1799-1802 and 1804-1816, a Dutch colony in the interval 1802-1804

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Suriname cell in 1800-1819 (its New Netherland row shows only Saint Martin in 1800-1802 and the Netherlands Antilles row starts at six islands). The pages: 'barring a period of British occupation between 1799 and 1802, and between 1804 and 1816' (infobox: 1804-1815).

correction.text: the coastal belt, returned to the Dutch in 1816 'after the defeat of Napoleon'

the whole of modern Suriname: Cliopatria's 1820 shape (524 of Suriname's 539 cells) without its 12 Guyana cells; the pages name no interior frontier and a 1954 constituent country of the Kingdom until independence in 1975

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, from the Netherlands Antilles row's wrong 1820-2023 shapes (see that dossier). The jump from the coastal belt (81 cells) to the whole country has no page and no year: Cliopatria makes it in 1820, but the colony was merged into the West Indies colony in 1828-1844 (no keyframe: the netherlands-antilles dossier draws Suriname then). The 12 Guyana cells (Corentyne) are not Suriname. Colony page: Suriname 'bordered British Guiana from 1831 to 1966'. The History page says the Maroon peace treaties 'granted them title to the lands': the interior was not effectively Dutch (soft).

region.text: Fort Willoughby, renamed Fort Zeelandia, and the English settlement on the Suriname River

ledger.note: 1667 (26 February): the Zeeland fleet attacks. 'The settlement was invaded by seven Dutch ships (from the Zeeland region), led by Abraham Crijnssen on 26 February 1667.' The English colony (Willoughbyland, founded 1650) had 'around 30,000 acres (120 km2)'.

region.text: the English colony of Francis Willoughby on the Suriname River, taken by the Dutch

ledger.note: 1667 (26 February): the Dutch take Surinam. 'Surinam was a Dutch colony from 26 February 1667, when Dutch forces captured' the English colony; the settlement was renamed Fort Zeelandia. The English recaptured it five months later under Admiral Sir John Harman, but news of the treaty reached it 'only weeks later' and it was returned to the Dutch (Willoughbyland page).

1667 (31 July): the Treaty of Breda. Dutch sovereignty over Surinam was 'kept in the Treaty of Breda of 31 July 1667'; the English kept New Netherland. 'Again confirmed in the Treaty of Westminster of 1674' (Surinam page); the English population was evacuated under Edward Cranfield in 1674 (History page). The New Netherland page calls the 1674 treaty an exchange 'in exchange for Suriname'; this page says only 'confirmed'.

1683: the Society of Suriname takes over. 'From 1683, the colony was governed by the Society of Suriname', three equal shareholders (the City of Amsterdam, the Van Aerssen van Sommelsdijck family and the West India Company); it 'came to an end in 1795'.
1795: the Society of Suriname ends: 'The Society came to an end in 1795 when this kind of trade and business was no longer seen as acceptable.'
1799: the British occupy Suriname. 'Suriname was occupied by the British in 1799' (History page); the Surinam page gives 1799-1802 and 1804-1816 (infobox: 1804-1815).

region.text: Surinam, back to the Dutch for two years

ledger.note: 1802: the first British occupation ends ('between 1799 and 1802').
1804: the second British occupation begins ('and between 1804 and 1816').
1816: Suriname 'was returned to the Dutch in 1816, after the defeat of Napoleon'. The Surinam page's infobox ends the second occupation in 1815, its text in 1816.

region.text: the interior of modern Suriname behind the plantation coast

ledger.note: 1820: Cliopatria extends the colony from the coastal belt (81 cells) to the whole of Suriname (524 cells). Neither page dates or describes the move; the History page says the Maroon treaties 'granted them title to the lands'. Page silent; the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Surinam, united with the colonies of Curaçao and Sint Eustatius

ledger.note: 1828: one West Indies colony. 'In 1828, Surinam was united with the colonies of Curaçao and Sint Eustatius', ruled from Paramaribo. Between 1828 and 1845 the netherlands-antilles dossier draws Suriname; this dossier has no keyframe.
1845: Surinam is separated again. 'The islands were separated in 1845 as the Colony of Curaçao', 'due to the distance between these territories.'

1954 (15 December): the Kingdom Charter. Surinam became a constituent country of the Kingdom ('the proclamation of the Charter for the Kingdom of the Netherlands on 15 December 1954'); the History page says Suriname 'gained self-government, with the Netherlands retaining control of defence and foreign affairs'.

1975 (25 November): independence. 'In 1975, Suriname left the Kingdom of the Netherlands to become the independent country' (Surinam page); independence 'was granted on 25 November 1975' (History page). Cliopatria's Republic of Suriname row starts in 1976.

wars.name: Dutch conquest of Surinam (Second Anglo-Dutch War)

zones.text: the English settlement on the Suriname River, 30,000 acres

wars.outcome: Dutch capture on 26 February 1667, English recapture five months later, return to the Dutch after the Treaty of Breda (31 July 1667); the Treaty of Westminster (1674) confirmed Dutch Suriname.
wars.note: The war's own article was not opened; the pages call it the attack of 1667 and the Treaty of Breda.

wars.name: British occupation of Suriname
wars.outcome: British occupation 1799-1802 and 1804-1816; the colony returned to the Dutch in 1816 'after the defeat of Napoleon'.
wars.note: The infobox gives 1804-1815 for the second period, the text 1804-1816.

certainty.note: The plantation belt had no surveyed edge and the interior stayed in Maroon and Indigenous hands ('peace treaties ... granted them title to the lands'); the pages date no boundary agreement with French Guiana (Marowijne) or British Guiana (Corantijn). Rivers form the coast-to-coast limits but the pages do not say they were agreed.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row. Suriname 1667-1975 has no Cliopatria state of its own: its coastal belt (81 cells) sits inside the New Netherland row 1670-1799 and the whole country (524 cells) inside the Netherlands Antilles row 1820-2023; both are marked wrong for Suriname in their own dossiers and replaced by this one. The Republic of Suriname row (am-08) starts in 1976. Written by am-06-c as a direct counterpart of netherlands-antilles (merge 1828, split 1845); a reviewer should check against the am-08 dossier for the republic. Interior frontier, the Corantijn/Marowijne limits and the 1820 expansion are not on the three pages opened. The New Netherland page says the 1674 treaty gave New Netherland up 'in exchange for Suriname'; the Surinam page says only that it 'confirmed' Dutch Suriname; Willoughbyland says 'de facto exchanged'. Wikidata id left null (not on the pages). Page budget: three pages.
